sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: It's the end of the year and time for our annual mini-stories episodes.
sentences.zh: 年关将至，又到了我们一年一度的迷你故事特辑时间。

sentences.en: Mini-stories are quick hit stories that were maybe pitched to us from someone in the audience
sentences.zh: 迷你故事是一些精简短小的故事，可能是听众向我们推荐的，

sentences.en: or something interesting we saw on Twitter,
sentences.zh: 或者我们在推特上看到的有趣内容，

sentences.en: or just a cool tidbit that we found in our research that just got stuck in our heads and wouldn't come out.
sentences.zh: 又或者只是我们在做研究时发现的一个酷炫趣闻，一直盘旋在脑海里挥之不去。

sentences.en: But they didn't quite warrant the full episode treatment for whatever reason.
sentences.zh: 但由于种种原因，它们还不足以撑起整整一期节目。

sentences.en: They're also this great opportunity for us to get to know the non-scripted version of the fine people who work on this show.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，这也是一个绝佳的机会，让我们得以了解这个节目的幕后优秀工作者们非剧本化的一面。

sentences.en: And as the person who gets to interview them, that is my favorite part of this.
sentences.zh: 作为负责采访他们的人，这是我最喜欢的部分。

sentences.en: We have some real charmers on staff.
sentences.zh: 我们员工里有几个极具魅力的人。

sentences.en: We'll have stories of mysterious ice boats, green ruins, sack dresses, steampunk violins,
sentences.zh: 我们将讲述关于神秘冰船、绿色废墟、面粉袋连衣裙、蒸汽朋克小提琴的故事，

sentences.en: and a little update from a couple of the notable city flags that have been redesigned around the country.
sentences.zh: 以及全国各地一些经过重新设计的著名城市旗帜的最新进展。

sentences.en: It's going to be fun.
sentences.zh: 这一定会很有趣。

sentences.en: First up is senior producer Katie Mingle.
sentences.zh: 首先登场的是资深制作人凯蒂·明格尔。

sentences.en: So, okay, we're going to start out by meeting Denise.
sentences.zh: 那么，好，我们首先来认识一下丹尼斯。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Denise Boniface,
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫丹尼斯·博尼法斯，

sentences.en: and I own Aquanuts Diving in Rocky Mountain House, Alberta, Canada.
sentences.zh: 我在加拿大艾伯塔省落基山ハウス经营一家名为Aquanuts Diving的潜水店。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Denise is from Alberta, Canada, where she owns a scuba diving company.
sentences.zh: 对，所以丹尼斯来自加拿大艾伯塔省，她在那里经营一家水肺潜水公司。

sentences.en: And Alberta, as you may know, is not a coastal province.
sentences.zh: 而你可能也知道，艾伯塔省并不是一个沿海省份。

sentences.en: So if you're scuba diving in Alberta, you're doing it in lakes.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在艾伯塔省潜水，你只能去湖里。

sentences.en: They're cold, they're dark, they're murky, they're kind of creepy.
sentences.zh: 那里水温冰冷、漆黑一片、浑浊不清，甚至还有点毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: It sounds delightful.
sentences.zh: 听起来真令人愉快。

sentences.en: Fun times.
sentences.zh: 真是好时光。

sentences.en: So there's this one lake called Lake Patricia.
sentences.zh: 有一个湖叫做帕特里夏湖。

sentences.en: Surrounded by mountains.
sentences.zh: 四周环山。

sentences.en: It's right in a mountain valley.
sentences.zh: 它就坐落在山谷里。

sentences.en: Very, very remote.
sentences.zh: 非常非常偏远。

sentences.en: And if you find the right spot on the lake and dive about 30 feet down, you'll find a shipwreck.
sentences.zh: 如果你在湖里找到合适的位置，下潜大约30英尺，你就会发现一艘沉船。

sentences.en: It doesn't really look like a ship.
sentences.zh: 它看起来其实不太像一艘船。

sentences.en: It looks like kind of there's a kind of pile of lumber that's all broken up and laying there.
sentences.zh: 它看起来更像是一堆七零八落躺在那里的木材。

sentences.en: And then there's a lot of refrigeration coils.
sentences.zh: 旁边还有许多制冷盘管。

sentences.en: What are the refrigeration coils for?
sentences.zh: 制冷盘管是用来做什么的？

sentences.en: We're going to get to that.
sentences.zh: 我们马上就会讲到。

sentences.en: But just, okay, for now, so you make your way down sort of through this murky darkness, this like pile of lumber and debris.
sentences.zh: 但现在，好吧，总之你顺着这种昏暗的光线一路下潜，穿过这堆木材和残骸。

sentences.en: 50 feet, 60 feet.
sentences.zh: 50英尺，60英尺。

sentences.en: And then you'll find a plaque.
sentences.zh: 然后你会发现一块牌匾。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: This is where Roman gets excited.
sentences.zh: 罗曼这就是来劲了。

sentences.en: It's pitch dark, but if you shine a light on it, you can read it.
sentences.zh: 里面漆黑一团，但如果你用手电筒照着它，就能读懂上面的字。

sentences.en: And Denise has read it.
sentences.zh: 丹尼斯已经读过了。

sentences.en: The plot says, Operation Habakkuk, a secret World War II project involving the use of ice in ship construction.
sentences.zh: 牌匾上写着：哈巴库克行动，一项在造船中使用冰的绝密二战计划。

sentences.en: This vessel built January to April 1943 was a prototype.
sentences.zh: 这艘船建于1943年1月至4月，是一个原型机。

sentences.en: For more information, contact the Canadian Park Service, Jasper.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请联系加拿大公园管理局，贾斯珀。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So there's like a hyperlink in the bottom of a lake.
sentences.zh: 所以湖底就像藏了一个超链接。

sentences.en: www.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a QR code.
sentences.zh: 对，还有一个二维码。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So there's so many things about this plaque that I love.
sentences.zh: 关于这块牌匾，有很多地方我都爱极了。

sentences.en: I love that it's at the bottom of a lake.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它位于湖底这一点。

sentences.en: I love the part where it says, for more info, contact the Canadian Park Service, because it sort of implies you could just stumble across this while, like,
sentences.zh: 我更喜欢上面写着“欲了解更多信息，请联系加拿大公园管理局”的部分，因为这仿佛暗示你只是在……闲逛时偶然发现了它，

sentences.en: strolling at the bottom of a Canadian lake.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大湖泊的底部散步。

sentences.en: And then I actually, I asked Denise that, and she was like, yeah, you could, because there's a lot of people that dive in this lake.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我问过丹尼斯这个问题，她说：“是的，你确实可能会，因为有很多人在这个湖里潜水。”

sentences.en: But, of course, the most intriguing part of the plaque is the part about the secret World War II project involving the use of ice in ship construction.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这块牌匾最吸引人的地方，还是关于那个在造船中使用冰的绝密二战计划的描述。

sentences.en: So what was that about?
sentences.zh: 那到底是怎么回事呢？

sentences.en: So, okay, so in the early 1940s, during World War II, German submarines, or U-boats as they were called, were basically wreaking havoc on Allied ships in the Atlantic Ocean,
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，在20世纪40年代初的二战期间，德国潜水艇（当时被称为U艇）在大西洋上对盟军船只大肆破坏，

sentences.en: just sinking them left and right.
sentences.zh: 把它们一艘接一艘地击沉。

sentences.en: And so eventually this person named Admiral Mountbatten goes to Winston Churchill, and he's like, we have to do something about this.
sentences.zh: 于是最后，一个叫蒙巴顿海军上将的人找到温斯顿·丘吉尔，对他说：“我们必须采取行动了。”

sentences.en: And I think I know what the solution is.
sentences.zh: “而且我想我知道解决方案是什么。”

sentences.en: A giant, unsinkable, aircraft carrier-sized ship made of ice.
sentences.zh: 一艘由冰制成的、巨大无比且永不沉没的航空母舰大小的巨轮。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 理所当然。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And actually Churchill is intrigued.
sentences.zh: 而且丘吉尔其实还挺感兴趣的。

sentences.en: Like, it sounds like one of those far-fetched ideas that kind of gets floated during times of war but never actually gets built, except for this really did get built,
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是战争时期经常冒出来、但最终从未真正建造的那些异想天开的想法之一，不过这个项目确实被建造了，

sentences.en: or at least a prototype of it got built.
sentences.zh: 或者至少建造了一个原型机。

sentences.en: And that is the shipwreck at the bottom of Patricia Lake.
sentences.zh: 这就是帕特里夏湖底的沉船。

sentences.en: And that's what the plaque commemorates.
sentences.zh: 这也是那块牌匾所纪念的事物。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So what in the world made Admiral Mountbatten think that an unsinkable ship should be made of ice?
sentences.zh: 那么究竟是什么让蒙巴顿海军上将觉得应该用冰来造一艘永不沉没的船呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: So, like, what the hell?
sentences.zh: 所以，到底搞什么鬼？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: That's fair enough.
sentences.zh: 这倒也合情合理。

sentences.en: Okay, so steel and aluminum were in really short supply.
sentences.zh: 当时钢和铝严重短缺。

sentences.en: So that was a big thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个重大问题。

sentences.en: They were actively looking for alternatives.
sentences.zh: 他们在积极寻找替代品。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then the second thing is that they hoped that this ice ship would be so dense that it would basically be indestructible.
sentences.zh: 其次，他们希望这种冰船能够足够密实，以至于基本上不可摧毁。

sentences.en: And what made them think that ice would be indestructible?
sentences.zh: 是什么让他们觉得冰会是不可摧毁的呢？

sentences.en: Because it doesn't seem like that.
sentences.zh: 因为看起来并不像那样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Yeah, it actually, it wasn't just plain ice.
sentences.zh: 其实，它并不仅仅是普通的冰。

sentences.en: They were going to build these ships out of a mixture of ice and sawdust called Pycrete, named after its inventor, a guy named Jeffrey Pike.
sentences.zh: 他们打算用一种由冰和木屑混合而成的名为“派克冰”（Pycrete）的材料来建造这些船，这个名字是以其发明者杰弗里·派克（Jeffrey Pike）的名字命名的。

sentences.en: So if you mixed sort of water and wood chips together and then froze it, it made the ice really, really strong.
sentences.zh: 如果你把水和木屑混合在一起然后冷冻，它会让冰变得非常非常坚固。

sentences.en: And so this guy, Jeffrey Pike, he invented not only Pycrete, but he came up with the idea of building a ship out of it.
sentences.zh: 所以这个叫杰弗里·派克的人，不仅发明了派克冰，还想出了用它来造船的主意。

sentences.en: And then he got that idea to Admiral Mountbatten.
sentences.zh: 然后他把这个想法带给了蒙巴顿海军上将。

sentences.en: So the ships would be built from blocks of Pycrete, and then there would basically be pipes with coolant running through the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 这些船将由派克冰块建造，然后在整个船体中穿设带有冷却剂的管道。

sentences.en: To keep it ice.
sentences.zh: 为了保持冰冻状态。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's the refrigerator coils that Denise saw at the bottom of the lake.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是丹尼斯在湖底看到的那些制冷盘管。

sentences.en: And Pycrete really was this, like, incredibly strong and dense mixture.
sentences.zh: 派克冰确实是一种非常坚固且致密的混合物。

sentences.en: And there's this amazing anecdote in this story where Admiral Mountbatten, who, again, is not the inventor of Pycrete, but he's, like, the main kind of evangelist for this idea.
sentences.zh: 这个故事里有一个令人惊叹的轶事：蒙巴顿海军上将，他再次强调并不是派克冰的发明者，但他可以说是这个想法的主要狂热推销员。

sentences.en: And he was so hype about it that he brings a piece of Pycrete to a meeting.
sentences.zh: 他对这个项目充满热情，以至于带了一块派克冰去参加一个会议。

sentences.en: This is a meeting in which they were trying to convince the Americans, so the British were trying to convince the Americans to get on board this crazy ice ship plan.
sentences.zh: 这是一场他们试图说服美国人的会议，英国人正试图说服美国人加入这个疯狂的冰船计划。

sentences.en: So he brings a block of Pycrete to the meeting along with a regular block of ice.
sentences.zh: 因此，他带了一块派克冰和一块普通的冰去开会。

sentences.en: And at some point, he does this demonstration where he takes out his revolver, and he shoots the regular ice, and it splinters into a thousand little pieces.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，他做了一个示范：他掏出左轮手枪，朝普通冰开了一枪，冰瞬间碎成了上千个小碎片。

sentences.en: And then he shoots the Pycrete, and the bullet bounces off the Pycrete and actually sort of ricochets into the leg of one of his colleagues.
sentences.zh: 然后他朝派克冰开枪，子弹从派克冰上弹了回来，竟然反弹到了他其中一个同事的腿上。

sentences.en: And, like, it's actually, like, declared a total success, and they're all, like, thumbs up, like, green light, full speed ahead.
sentences.zh: 然后，这实际上被宣布为一次巨大的成功，他们都竖起大拇指，表示绿灯放行，全速前进。

sentences.en: And, yeah, they decide to go forward with this crazy plan.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们决定继续推进这个疯狂的计划。

sentences.en: Winston Churchill signs off on it.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿·丘吉尔签字批准了。

sentences.en: I'm not sure what all Americans signed off on it, but the Americans said, we'll help you do this.
sentences.zh: 我不确定具体有哪些美国人批准了，但美国人说：“我们会帮你们完成这个。”

sentences.en: And then I guess at some point they also got Canadians involved because they end up building this prototype on this little lake in Alberta, Canada.
sentences.zh: 然后我想他们在某个时候还让加拿大人参与进来了，因为他们最终在加拿大艾伯塔省的一个小湖里建造了这个原型。

sentences.en: Lake Patricia.
sentences.zh: 帕特里夏湖。

sentences.en: Yes, Lake Patricia.
sentences.zh: 是的，帕特里夏湖。

sentences.en: And they name it Project Habakkuk after a Bible verse.
sentences.zh: 他们根据圣经经文将之命名为“哈巴库克计划”。

sentences.en: And I think the verse is pretty interesting, so I'm going to read it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这段经文挺有意思的，所以我要念一下。

sentences.en: It goes,
sentences.zh: 它是这么说的：

sentences.en: Behold ye among the nations, and look, and wonder marvelously, for I am working a work in your days, which ye will not believe, though it be told to you.
sentences.zh: “你们要在列国中观看，要大大惊奇；因为在你们的日子里，我将行一件奇事，虽有人告诉你们，你们总是不信。”

sentences.en: It's basically, like, the Bible verse that's, like, we are building a crazy f***ing thing.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是那种《圣经》经文，意思是：我们在造一个他妈的疯狂东西。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢。

sentences.en: And Habakkuk apparently was the name of a Hebrew prophet, which I certainly never knew.
sentences.zh: 显然哈巴库克是一个希伯来先知的名字，这一点我以前确实不知道。

sentences.en: And then the prototype itself was built by Canadian conscientious objectors who didn't know what they were building and who had opted for alternative service jobs.
sentences.zh: 而这个原型本身是由加拿大的宗教兵役拒服兵役者建造的，他们当时并不知道自己在建造什么，只是选择了替代性的服务工作。

sentences.en: And they were, like, given this job and not really told that it actually was a warship.
sentences.zh: 他们被指派了这项工作，但并没有被告知这其实是一艘军舰。

sentences.en: Yeah, for the war.
sentences.zh: 是的，为了战争。

sentences.en: So in just a few months, they built a prototype of this ship, but it ended up being harder to build and more expensive than they thought.
sentences.zh: 因此，在短短几个月内，他们就建造了这个船只的原型，但结果发现建造难度比想象中更大，成本也更高。

sentences.en: And by the time the prototype was ready, the war had kind of moved on.
sentences.zh: 等到原型机准备就绪时，战争的形势已经发生了变化。

sentences.en: Like, they were figuring out how to build the atomic bomb.
sentences.zh: 比如说，他们当时正在研究如何制造原子弹。

sentences.en: They figured out how to mass produce smaller aircraft carriers.
sentences.zh: 他们已经弄清楚了如何批量生产较小的航空母舰。

sentences.en: And in the end, they basically scrapped the project and ultimately let it sink into the bottom of Lake Patricia.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们基本上废弃了这个项目，并最终让它沉入了帕特里夏湖底。

sentences.en: And as we know, you can still see it there today.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，今天你依然能在那里看到它。

sentences.en: Well, the coolest thing about diving the Habakkuk is being able to say that you dove the Habakkuk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，潜水探索哈巴库克号最酷的事情，就是能够跟别人说你潜水探索过哈巴库克号。

sentences.en: Like, it is cool to dive it, and it's nice to see it once.
sentences.zh: 去潜水确实很酷，去参观一次也不错。

sentences.en: But to dive it too many times, it's not that interesting.
sentences.zh: 但如果去潜水太多次，也就没那么大意思了。

sentences.en: But I'm not a word to it, but that doesn't really help your prettier program, does it?
sentences.zh: 但我并不是这方面的行家，不过这对你们的冰船项目其实没什么帮助，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So apparently, like, if you build a ship out of ice, it just sort of, like, turns into nothing.
sentences.zh: 所以显然，如果你用冰造一艘船，它最后就会……化为乌有。

sentences.en: Or slushed at the bottom of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 或者变成海底的冰泥浆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And if you've seen it once, you've seen it enough.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过一次，你就看够了。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: That's awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I love that story.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个故事。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Debbie Schneiderman, who sent in the tip about Project Habakkuk.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢黛比·施奈德曼，她提供了关于哈巴库克计划的线索。

sentences.en: She actually sent it in response to the mini-stories episode that we did last year.
sentences.zh: 她其实是在回应我们去年制作的迷你故事节目时发来的。

sentences.en: So if you also have a mini-story suggestion, we do read them.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你也有迷你故事的建议，我们确实会看。

sentences.en: Reach us through the contact page at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 请通过99pi.org的联系页面与我们取得联系。

sentences.en: Next up, producer Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 接下来是制作人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Are you ready?
sentences.zh: 准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you should just start.
sentences.zh: 行，你直接开始吧。

sentences.en: Because I don't know what you're going to do.
sentences.zh: 因为我不知道你要搞什么鬼。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So this is a story about a ruin.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个关于废墟的故事。

sentences.en: It's probably the most famous ruin, maybe, in the world.
sentences.zh: 它可能是世界上最著名的废墟了。

sentences.en: The Roman Colosseum.
sentences.zh: 罗马斗兽场。

sentences.en: Oh, cool.
